page: Amazon Web Services m7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. It features 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 3.7 GHz, utilizing a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. The memory configuration consists of 256 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, providing a balanced 4 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on the AWS Nitro hypervisor to manage resources and network-attached storage. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights the instance's strong multi-core and memory performance. In multi-core processing, the m7a.16xlarge achieves top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and software compilation tasks. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks also ranks in the top 10%, while large-block read and write operations fall within the top 25%. Single-core performance is strong, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core scores placing in the top 25%. For specialized workloads, the CPU's instruction set supports AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration, contributing to strong performance in database operations and medium-model LLM text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m7a.16xlarge offers high resource density and modern DDR5 memory performance without the overhead of bundled local storage or GPUs. This makes it a qualitatively cost-effective choice for workloads that scale horizontally and rely on network-attached storage. The instance is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
